result.title: Preventing Model Extraction in Contextual Linear Optimization
result.summary: Consider a contextual linear optimization problem, where a predict-then-optimize (PTO) system returns optimal decisions without revealing the cost vectors used in its downstream linear program. Our focus is on how to prevent attackers, who can submit context queries, from extracting the underlying prediction model. Although the cost-to-decision map is many-to-one, observations across contexts can reveal the underlying prediction model. For linear models, we provide sufficient conditions where the attacker can learn the model up to positive scaling by only observing the decision. These conditions motivate an adaptive attack that alternates inverse optimization with boundary sampling, i.e., using context queries leading to decision boundaries of the current attacker model. To prevent extraction, we propose a mechanism that perturbs decisions only when the predicted cost vector is near a decision boundary. We establish a regret bound in terms of the perturbation radius. For the attackers that fit the defended responses as optimal decisions under the evaluation distribution, we also prove a lower bound on expected extraction error. Experiments on synthetic instances and real data quantify the security-performance trade-off of the defense mechanism and illustrate that our defense can increase the extraction error.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 predict-then-optimize 系统如何防止攻击者仅凭提交 context 查询、观察返回决策来提取底层预测模型：给出线性模型可被恢复至正缩放的充分条件，据此设计 inverse optimization 与决策边界采样交替的自适应攻击，并提出只在预测代价向量接近决策边界时扰动决策的防御，配以 regret 界与提取误差下界及合成、真实数据实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 「多对一的代价到决策映射仍可暴露内部模型」的可辨识性分析与边界采样式主动探测，可能为 LVR 中判断最终答案是否真正用到 latent 内容、以及沿决策边界构造探针来检验视觉证据作用提供概念参照，可供核查但迁移性未验证。
